_comment: Applied by FusionAuth only against an empty database, on first boot.
Why this file exists: the OAuth client id and secret must agree in two places at once —
inside FusionAuth, and in the docker.env the two OpenVPS apps read. Configuring
FusionAuth by hand and copying the generated values into Secrets Manager is a
chicken-and-egg dance that has to be repeated on every rebuild. Instead the values are
generated once into Secrets Manager, and this file tells FusionAuth to adopt them.
#{ENV.X} is substituted by FusionAuth from the container environment, which user-data
populates from Secrets Manager. Nothing secret lives in this file or in git.
Request order matters: kickstart executes them in sequence, so the application must
exist before anything can be registered to it.
Redirect URLs must match the public app URLs EXACTLY or login fails with a
misconfiguration error — the most common way to break this deployment.
The tenant issuer is NOT set here. #{defaultTenantId} is not an implicit kickstart
variable — referencing it aborts the ENTIRE kickstart with 'You may not use an
undefined variable', leaving no api key and no application. It is set from the API
by openvps-fusionauth-configure once FusionAuth is up.

requests._comment: 1. The OpenVPS application, adopting the client id/secret from Secrets Manager.
2. Admin user, registered to FusionAuth's own admin app so the console is reachable.
3. Same user registered to the OpenVPS application, so they can actually log in to it.
